ambiguities.text: The specification does not define how chain ID is updated during a contentious split.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume chain ID changes require a hard fork and are configured at the node level, not dynamically changeable at runtime.

ambiguities.text: The term 'trustless oracles' for chain ID change detection is mentioned but not defined.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume this refers to on-chain mechanisms or multi-sig governance that can signal chain ID changes.

implicit_assumptions.description: The chain ID configured on the node matches the canonical chain ID for the network.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Contracts would validate signatures against wrong chain ID, either accepting replays or rejecting valid transactions.

implicit_assumptions.description: EIP-155 transaction signing uses the same chain ID returned by CHAINID opcode.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Inconsistency between transaction validation and contract-level checks could create replay windows.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot cause the chain ID to change without network-wide consensus.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Chain ID manipulation could enable replay attacks or signature invalidation attacks.
